chain.label: Discrete dirty white spot in HPT stage 2 disk forging
chain.trigger: a discrete region underneath the largest discontinuity that appeared white compared with the surrounding material... referred to collectively as a 'discrete dirty white spot'

chain.label: Production ultrasonic inspections could not detect the stealth anomaly
chain.trigger: the discrete dirty white spot was most likely not detectable by the ultrasonic inspection methods used during production of the HPT stage 2 disk

caused_by.evidence: consistent with the description of a 'stealth' anomaly... the lack of cracking and voiding, combined with a similarity in elastic modulus and density to the parent alloy, renders them indistinguishable from the parent alloy for sonic detection

chain.label: Low-cycle fatigue cracks initiated and grew from the anomaly
chain.trigger: multiple cracks initiating along the edges of the discontinuities... consistent with crack growth by low-cycle fatigue

caused_by.evidence: The stringers of oxide and nitride particles associated with a discrete dirty white spot are known to act as initiation sites for fatigue cracks, significantly reducing the low-cycle fatigue life of alloy 718
ATI SM detected no anomalies during its ultrasonic inspection of the billet involved in this event... MTU found no anomalies during the ultrasonic inspection of the forged pieces

chain.label: AD-mandated in-service inspections only surface/near-surface capable
chain.trigger: These inspection techniques were not capable of detecting the cracks that emanated from the discrete dirty white spot (a subsurface anomaly) because they could only detect cracks and other anomalies at the surface (FPI) and near the surface (ECI)

caused_by.evidence: the cracks remained below the material's surface when American Airlines inspected the disk during the engine's January 2011 maintenance

chain.label: Uncontained rupture of right engine HPT stage 2 disk on takeoff roll
chain.trigger: an uncontained engine failure in the right engine and subsequent fire occurred... The uncontained engine failure resulted from a high-pressure turbine (HPT) stage 2 disk rupture

caused_by.evidence: The HPT stage 2 disk failed because of low-cycle fatigue cracks that initiated from an internal subsurface manufacturing anomaly
If a subsurface ultrasonic inspection had been required at the time of the disk's last inspection, the cracks that developed from the discrete dirty white spot would most likely have been detectable

chain.label: Disk fragment severed fuel feed line and breached right wing fuel tank
chain.trigger: One fragment penetrated through the inboard section of the right wing, severed the main engine fuel feed line, breached the fuel tank

caused_by.evidence: a disk fragment, along with smaller engine hardware fragments, impacted the right engine, right wing, and portions of the right fuselage, severing the main engine fuel feed line and breaching the right-wing fuel tank

chain.label: Fuel-fed fire on right side of airplane and smoke in cabin
chain.trigger: releasing fuel that resulted in a fire on the right side of the airplane during the takeoff roll

caused_by.evidence: allowed fuel to flow into the dry bay and out of the hole of the wing... the released amount ignited, resulting in a fire that... caused the cabin to fill with smoke

chain.label: Flight attendants lacked hands-on interphone training for installed model
chain.trigger: the subject was presented during recurrent training without providing flight attendants with hands-on experience using an interphone during an emergency

chain.label: No communication between flight and cabin crews after the airplane stopped
chain.trigger: The flight crew did not communicate with the flight attendants to relay its intent not to immediately evacuate... none of the flight attendants activated the signaling system, and only two of the seven flight attendants attempted (unsuccessfully) to communicate with the flight crew

caused_by.evidence: the flight attendants initiated an evacuation... due to the severity of the fire on the right side of the airplane
one flight attendant tried to use the interphone to alert the flight crew that the left engine was still operating but was unsuccessful because she operated the interphone incorrectly

chain.label: Engine fire checklist did not differentiate ground from in-flight operations
chain.trigger: the engine fire checklist did not differentiate between an engine fire in flight and an engine fire while the airplane was on the ground and did not include a step, for an engine fire on the ground, to shut down the unaffected engine

chain.label: Left overwing exit opened and used while left engine still operating
chain.trigger: another flight attendant stationed on the left side of the airplane assessed the conditions outside the airplane yet opened the left overwing exit while the engine was still operating

caused_by.evidence: his main concern was getting passengers off the airplane because of the fire
the design of the engine fire checklist delayed initiating the evacuation checklist, shutting down the left engine, and commanding an evacuation from the cockpit
Contributing to the delay in shutting down the left engine was... the lack of communication between the flight and cabin crews after the airplane came to a stop

chain.label: Serious injury from jet blast plus 20 minor injuries in evacuation
chain.trigger: the passenger stood up to get away from the airplane but was knocked down by the jet blast coming from the left engine

caused_by.evidence: The one serious injury that resulted during the evacuation occurred after a passenger evacuated using the left overwing exit
